designTheme.label: Advanced theme · design language
designTheme.description: A second axis next to the color theme. It replaces the whole design language — color roles, shape, elevation, typography, motion, state layers and component geometry. Every number comes from Google's own generated Material 3 token dictionary (@material/web, design system v0.192); nothing here is typed from memory.

native.label: Native (Xiranite styling)
native.description: No design language is applied. The color theme and the built-in component styling stay exactly as they are.

md3.label: Material 3
md3.description: Material You color roles from a source color, plus M3 shape, elevation, type scale, motion curves, state layers and per-component metrics.

mondrian.label: De Stijl · Mondrian
mondrian.description: Neoplasticism: only primary colours and non-colours, only rectangles and straight horizontal/vertical lines, zero radius, zero shadow, feedback by opposition. Colours are measured from public-domain reproductions; every token records its own source.

wuling.label: Wuling · Jade Industrial
wuling.description: The app's own Wuling preset promoted to a design language: hard offset shadows with no blur, a 2/4/8px corner ladder, ledger-style mono labels, one 180ms curve and a blueprint grid. Every value is measured from the surviving preset with its line number, so the default tiers look exactly like the preset today.

swiss.label: Swiss · International Typographic
swiss.description: International Typographic Style (Zurich, 1950s) on SBB's published numbers: zero radius everywhere, hierarchy carried by hairlines and background steps instead of shadow, one functional red, two weights only, and grid/dot textures for depth. Values come from the SBB design system v5.2.0 and the Swiss-Minimalist composition brief; the colour axis deliberately has no picker - there is only one red, and it is a signal.

lonestar.label: Lone Star · 孤星
lonestar.description: Arknights 孤星 as a cassette-futurism skin on the same bones: two grounds only (a polyester-tinted paper over a machine chassis), a high-brightness orange reserved for mechanical interaction, 45° cut corners instead of fillets, monospaced tabular figures, and selection that is always the contract's cyan - never that orange. Nobody publishes the event's hex values, so every colour here is a calibration against its four documented properties; the settings panel says so out loud.

designTheme.ledgerLabelsDesc: Mono, uppercase, tracked small labels on badges and table heads
designTheme.noSeedNote: There is deliberately no colour picker here: this language has exactly one accent, and that accent is a signal colour (SBB brand and product roles resolve to the same red). A swatch that changes nothing would be a lie.
designTheme.upperLabelsDesc: Uppercase + tracking on badges and table heads only; body copy keeps its grammar
designTheme.monoFiguresDesc: Digits and identifiers set in the app mono with tabular numerals so columns align on the digit
designTheme.cutNote: Cut corners are fixed by the token contract: 6px on panels, 12px on lifted blocks - one cut treatment per component, so there is no slider here.
designTheme.swissProvenanceNote: Font families and sizes stay with the colour theme, the font preset and your zoom: this language only multiplies the size that is already in effect (ADR-0080). Per-token sources: docs/advanced-design-theme-md3.md §13.
designTheme.lonestarProvenanceNote: No official colour list exists for this event. These values are a calibration against four documented properties plus the extracted token contract, inherited from the sister project that already shipped them - see docs/advanced-design-theme-md3.md §14.
designTheme.provenanceNote: Numbers marked as UI translations (line width, spacing, type sizes) have no documented De Stijl value — see docs/advanced-design-theme-md3.md.
